data.gender_notes: Joshvika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Joshvika is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Josh', which means 'Goddess of wealth and prosperity'. In Hindu mythology, Josh is a manifestation of the Goddess Lakshmi. The name is believed to bring wealth, abundance, and good fortune to the one who bears it. The name Joshvika carries the meaning “Goddess of wealth and prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Joshvika usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of wealth and prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Joshvika was a celebrated poetess in ancient India, who sang the praises of Lord Vishnu. The name Joshvika carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Alvars were a group of Shaiva saints in medieval Tamilakam who revered Shiva as the supreme deity. Joshvika, a Vaishnavite poetess, composed poems extolling Vishnu and the Alvar saints. Her works were included in the 12 Vaishnava Agamas.

historical_references.reference: Joshvika is also mentioned in later medieval Hindu literature as a disciple of the great philosopher Ramanuja.
historical_references.context: Ramanuja, a prominent figure in Hindu philosophy, founded the Sri Vaishnavite tradition which emphasized the supremacy of Vishnu. Joshvika is said to have been a prominent female disciple who contributed significantly to this tradition through her devotional poetry.
